title: Single-Area OSPFv3 for IPv6
summary: Implement and verify single-area Open Shortest Path First version 3 (OSPFv3) for IPv6 across a three-router enterprise topology, establish router IDs, configure point-to-point transit adjacencies, apply passive interfaces, and verify route convergence.
learning_objectives: Explain the key architectural differences between OSPFv2 (IPv4) and OSPFv3 (IPv6), including link-local next-hop addressing and interface-level activation
Configure 32-bit dotted-decimal OSPFv3 Router IDs on Cisco IOS routers
Activate OSPFv3 Area 0 directly on physical transit, LAN, and loopback interfaces
Configure point-to-point OSPFv3 network types on inter-router links to optimize adjacency formation and eliminate DR/BDR overhead
Apply passive-interface directives to customer-facing LAN segments to suppress unnecessary multicast traffic
Inspect OSPFv3 neighbor adjacencies, Link-State database (LSAs), and learned IPv6 routing tables using Cisco IOS verification commands
Verify bidirectional end-to-end IPv6 packet forwarding across multi-hop OSPFv3 routing domains

source.origin: Independently authored enterprise IPv6 dynamic routing curriculum guide aligned with Cisco CCNA exam topic 3.2 (Configure and verify single area OSPFv2 / OSPFv3) and enterprise dual-stack standards
